title.zh: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢
title.en: Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing
title.raw: 卷一百五十六 列傳第八十一 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢 Volume 156 Biographies 81: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing

sentences.zh: 楊戴陽二李韓杜邢

translations.literal: Yang, Dai, Yang, two Li's, Han, Du, Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, Dai, Yang, the two Lis, Han, Du, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟

translations.literal: Yang Chaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaosheng

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟，字叔明，夏州朔方人。

translations.literal: Yang Chaosheng, courtesy name Shuming, was a native of Shuofang in Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaosheng, whose courtesy name was Shuming, came from Shuofang in Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 興行間，以先鋒功授甘泉府果毅。

translations.literal: At the time of the Xingxing campaign, he was appointed defender of Ganquan-fu for his achievements as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xingxing operations he distinguished himself in the vanguard and was appointed defender of Ganquan-fu.

sentences.zh: 建中初，從李懷光討劉文喜涇州，斬獲多，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he followed Li Huai'guang to attack Liu Wenxi at Jing Prefecture, taking many heads and captives; he was promoted to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era he campaigned with Li Huai'guang against Liu Wenxi at Jingzhou, winning heavy slayings and captures, and was promoted to Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李納寇徐州，從唐朝臣往討，常冠軍。

translations.literal: When Li Na raided Xuzhou, he went with Tang Chaochen to repel him and often led the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na raided Xuzhou, he marched with Tang Chaochen to drive him off and repeatedly took first place in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 懷光赴難奉天，屬朝晟兵千人下咸陽，賜實封百五十戶。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang went to relieve Fengtian, Chaosheng was left with a thousand troops below Xianyang and granted a hundred fifty households of hereditary fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang hurried to the rescue at Fengtian, Chaosheng was left in command of a thousand men below Xianyang and granted an actual fief of one hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 懷光反，韓遊瑰退保邠、寧，賊黨張昕守邠州，大索軍實，多募士，欲潛歸之。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang rebelled, Han Yougui withdrew to hold Bin and Ning; the rebel adherent Zhang Xin held Bin Prefecture, searched extensively for military supplies, recruited many soldiers, and wished secretly to join him.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang rebelled, Han Yougui fell back to defend Bin and Ning, while the rebel partisan Zhang Xin held Binzhou, scoured the armies for supplies, drafted many men, and plotted to defect to Huai'guang in secret.

sentences.zh: 朝晟父懷賓為遊瑰將，夜以數十騎斬昕及同謀者。

translations.literal: Chaosheng's father Huaiyin was a general under Yougui; by night with several dozen riders he beheaded Xin and his fellow conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng's father Huaiyin served under Yougui as a general; one night he rode out with several dozen horsemen and killed Xin and the other conspirators.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰遣懷賓告行在，德宗勞問，授兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Yougui sent Huaiyin to report to the traveling court; Dezong rewarded and questioned him, appointing him concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui dispatched Huaiyin to report to the imperial camp; Dezong received him warmly and named him concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 朝晟泣見懷光曰：「父立功於國，子當誅，不可以主兵。

translations.literal: Chaosheng wept and saw Huai'guang, saying: "My father has achieved merit for the state; the son ought to be executed; he cannot command troops."
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng came before Huai'guang in tears and said, "My father has won merit for the realm, and as his son I deserve execution — I must not be allowed to lead soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」懷光縶之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang had him bound.

sentences.zh: 及諸軍圍河中，遊瑰營長春宮，而懷賓戰甚力。

translations.literal: When the various armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui encamped at Changchun Palace, while Huaiyin fought with great force.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies besieged Hezhong, Yougui pitched camp at Changchun Palace while Huaiyin fought with relentless vigor.

sentences.zh: 懷光平，帝原朝晟，因為遊瑰都虞候。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang was pacified, the Emperor pardoned Chaosheng and made him Yougui's Chief Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang's rebellion was crushed, the emperor pardoned Chaosheng and appointed him chief adjutant under Yougui.

sentences.zh: 父子皆開府、賓客、御史中丞，軍中以為榮。

translations.literal: Father and son both held establishments as honorary officials, guest ministers, and Vice Censors-in-Chief; within the army this was regarded as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son alike held honorary grand-secretary ranks, guest-minister titles, and Vice Censor-in-Chief posts — a distinction the army took as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯邊，遊瑰自將守寧州，而禦士寬，軍驕。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided the frontier, Yougui personally led troops to guard Ning Prefecture, but his discipline of the soldiers was lax and the army grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the border, Yougui took personal command at Ningzhou, but his discipline was lax and the troops grew insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 及張獻甫來代，軍遂亂，朝晟逃於郊。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianfu came to replace him, the army thereupon mutinied, and Chaosheng fled to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianfu arrived to replace him, the army mutinied, and Chaosheng fled into the countryside.

sentences.zh: 眾脅監軍，請以范希朝為節度使。

translations.literal: The masses coerced the army supervisor and requested Fan Xichao as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers seized the army supervisor and demanded that Fan Xichao be made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 希朝時已在京師。

translations.literal: Xichao was then already in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao was already in the capital at the time.

sentences.zh: 明日，朝晟出，紿眾曰：「予來賀所請之當也。

translations.literal: The next day Chaosheng came out and deceived the masses, saying: "I have come to congratulate you on the appropriateness of your request."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chaosheng appeared and told the troops, "I have come to congratulate you on making the right choice."

sentences.zh: 」眾稍定。

translations.literal: The masses were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The men gradually settled down.

sentences.zh: 朝晟結諸將謀誅首惡者。

translations.literal: Chaosheng joined the various generals in plotting to execute the chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng rallied the other generals to plot the execution of the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 居三日，紿遣人自邠來，曰：「前請報罷，張公已舍邠矣，反者皆當死，吾不願盡誅也，第取首惡者。

translations.literal: After three days he deceived them, sending a man from Bin, who said: "The previous request has been denied; Lord Zhang has already left Bin; all rebels ought to die; I do not wish to execute them all, but only take the chief evildoers."
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he staged a ruse, sending a messenger from Bin who announced, "Your petition has been rejected; Lord Zhang has already left Binzhou. All rebels deserve death, but I do not wish to slaughter everyone — only the ringleaders need die."

sentences.zh: 」眾所讙指，斬二百餘人，獻甫遂入於軍。

translations.literal: Those whom the masses cheered and pointed out were beheaded, more than two hundred persons; Xianfu thereupon entered the army.
translations.idiomatic: The men singled out more than two hundred ringleaders for execution, and Xianfu was then able to take command of the army.

sentences.zh: 帝以希朝為節度副使，而朝晟加御史大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Xichao deputy military commissioner, while Chaosheng was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Xichao deputy military commissioner and promoted Chaosheng to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年，城鹽州，發卒護境，朝晟屯木波堡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan, Salt Prefecture was fortified, troops were dispatched to guard the border, and Chaosheng encamped at Mubo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 9, when Salt Prefecture was fortified and troops were sent to guard the frontier, Chaosheng encamped at Mubo Fort.

sentences.zh: 會獻甫卒，有詔代為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Xianfu died, an edict appointed him to replace him as Binning military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfu died, an edict named Chaosheng military commissioner of Binning in his place.

sentences.zh: 朝晟請城方渠，合道，木波以遏吐蕃路。

translations.literal: Chaosheng requested to fortify Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to block the Tibetan route.
translations.idiomatic: Chaosheng proposed building fortresses at Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo to choke off the Tibetan advance routes.

sentences.zh: 詔問：「須兵幾何？

translations.literal: An edict asked: "How many troops are needed?"
translations.idiomatic: The throne asked, "How many troops will you need?"

sentences.zh: 」報曰：「部兵可辦。

translations.literal: He reported: "The troops of the command can manage it."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My own command can handle it."

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「前日城五原，興師七萬，今何易邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Previously when fortifying Wuyuan, seventy thousand troops were mobilized; why is it easy now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "When we fortified Wuyuan earlier we mobilized seventy thousand men — why is this so easy now?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「鹽州之役，虜先知之。

translations.literal: He replied: "In the Salt Prefecture campaign, the barbarians knew of it beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "At Salt Prefecture the enemy learned of our plans in advance."

sentences.zh: 今薄戎而城，虜料王師不十萬，勢難輕入。

translations.literal: Now, pressing close to the enemy while fortifying, the barbarians will reckon the imperial army at fewer than a hundred thousand and will find it difficult to enter lightly.
translations.idiomatic: This time we will build close to their territory; they will assume the imperial forces number fewer than a hundred thousand and will not dare to attack lightly.

sentences.zh: 若發部兵，十日至塞下，未三旬城畢，積芻聚糧，留卒守之，寇至不可拔，萊野翦夷，虜且走，此萬全計也。

translations.literal: If we dispatch the command troops, in ten days they reach below the pass; in less than thirty days the fortifications are complete; fodder and grain are accumulated; troops are left to guard; when the enemy comes they cannot take it; the fields and wilds are cleared; the barbarians will then flee — this is a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: If we send only my command troops, they can reach the frontier in ten days and finish the walls in under thirty. We stockpile fodder and grain, leave garrisons behind, and when the enemy arrives they cannot dislodge us. Once the countryside is cleared the barbarians will withdraw — that is a plan without flaw.

sentences.zh: 若大發兵，閱月乃至，虜亦來，來必戰，戰則不暇城矣。

translations.literal: If a great force is mobilized, after a month they arrive, the barbarians also come, coming they must fight, fighting then there is no leisure to fortify.
translations.idiomatic: If we mobilize a huge army, it takes a month to arrive — by then the enemy comes too, and once they come we must fight; if we are fighting we have no time to build walls.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其策。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 師次方渠，水乏。

translations.literal: The army halted at Fangqu; water was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Fangqu, water ran short.

sentences.zh: 有青蛇降險下走，視其跡，水從而流，朝晟使築防環之，遂為渟淵，士飲仰足，圖其事以聞。

translations.literal: A green serpent descended the precipice and went down; observing its tracks, water flowed along with it; Chaosheng had a dike built to encircle it, and it became a deep pool; the soldiers drank their fill; he illustrated the affair and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: A green serpent was seen slithering down a cliff; following its trail, water began to flow. Chaosheng had a retaining wall built around the spring, forming a deep pool from which the troops drank their fill. He sent a report illustrated with an account of the event.

sentences.zh: 有詔置祠，命泉曰應聖。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a shrine established and named the spring Responsive to the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a shrine erected and named the spring Responsive to the Sage.

sentences.zh: 已城，吐蕃悉眾至，度不能害，乃引去。

translations.literal: After the fortifications were complete, the Tibetans came with their entire force, judged they could not harm it, and thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once the walls were finished, the Tibetans came in full force, saw they could not overcome the position, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復城馬嶺而歸，開地三百里。

translations.literal: He again fortified Maling and returned, opening three hundred li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Maling as well and returned, opening three hundred li of new territory.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於屯。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at his encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏 弟戴休璿 戴休晏

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan; younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan; his younger brothers Dai Xiuxuan and Dai Xiuyan

sentences.zh: 戴休顏，字休顏，夏州人。

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan, courtesy name Xiuyan, was a man of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyan, came from Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家世尚武，誌膽不常。

translations.literal: His family for generations esteemed martial affairs; his ambition and courage were extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been martial in tradition, and his resolve and daring were out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引為大將，諭平党項羌，以安河曲。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi brought him in as a great general and instructed him to pacify the Tangut Qiang and secure the Hequ region.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi took him on as a senior commander and charged him with pacifying the Tangut Qiang to secure the Hequ frontier.

sentences.zh: 試太常卿，封濟陰郡公，進封咸寧郡王，兼朔方節度副使。

translations.literal: He was tried as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyin Commandery, advanced to Prince of Xianning Commandery, and concurrently made deputy military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He served provisionally as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was created Duke of Jiyin, then advanced to Prince of Xianning and appointed deputy military commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 城邠州功最，遷鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: His achievements in fortifying Bin Prefecture were foremost; he was transferred to be Regional Inspector of Salt Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His work on the Binzhou fortifications ranked first, and he was transferred to regional inspector of Salt Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，率兵三千晝夜馳，奔問行在，德宗嘉之，賜實戶二百。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he led three thousand troops day and night at full gallop to hurry to the traveling court; Dezong commended him and granted two hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he raced day and night with three thousand men to reach the imperial camp. Dezong praised him and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 與渾瑊、杜希全、韓遊瑰等扞禦有勞。

translations.literal: Together with Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he had merit in defending and resisting.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Hun Jian, Du Xiquan, Han Yougui, and others he distinguished himself in the defense.

sentences.zh: 帝進狩梁、洋，留守奉天。

translations.literal: The Emperor advanced to hunt in Liang and Yang; Xiuyan remained to guard Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Liang and Yang, Xiuyan stayed behind to hold Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 李懷光屯咸陽，使人誘之，休顏斬其使，勒兵自守。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang encamped at Xianyang and sent men to entice him; Xiuyan beheaded the envoy and marshaled troops to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang, encamped at Xianyang, sent envoys to win him over; Xiuyan executed the messengers and mobilized his troops to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 懷光眙駭，自涇陽夜走。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was stunned and fled by night from Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang was struck with dismay and fled Jingyang by night.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校工部尚書、奉天行營節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Fengtian field army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Fengtian field army.

sentences.zh: 合渾瑊兵破泚偏師，斬首三千級，追至中渭橋。

translations.literal: Joining with Hun Jian's troops he defeated Zhu Ci's detached force, taking three thousand heads, and pursued to the Middle Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Hun Jian's forces he routed a detached column of Zhu Ci's army, taking three thousand heads, and pursued as far as the Middle Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 京師平，又與瑊率兵趨岐陽，邀泚殘黨。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he again led troops with Jian toward Qiyang to intercept Zhu Ci's remnant adherents.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered, he marched with Jian toward Qiyang to cut off Zhu Ci's remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右僕射，進戶四百。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and advanced four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and his fief was increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從乘輿至京師，賜女樂、甲第，拜左龍武軍統軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage to the capital, was granted female musicians and a fine mansion, and appointed Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor back to the capital, received female musicians and a grand residence, and was named commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Protector of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Protector of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弟休璿，歷開府儀同三司，封東陽郡王；

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiuxuan successively served as Grand Master with Establishment Equal to the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiuxuan rose to Grand Master with Establishment Equal to the Three Excellencies and was created Prince of Dongyang;

sentences.zh: 休晏，歷輔國大將軍，封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Xiuyan successively served as Grand General Who Assists the State and was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyan rose to Grand General Who Assists the State and was created Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 俱以將略稱。

translations.literal: Both were famed for military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Both were renowned for their military ability.

sentences.zh: 陽惠元

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan

sentences.zh: 陽惠元，平州人。

translations.literal: Yang Huiyuan was a man of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huiyuan came from Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以趫勇奮，事平盧軍。

translations.literal: For his swift courage and vigor he served in the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Known for his swift courage, he served in the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 從田神功、李忠臣浮海入青州。

translations.literal: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen across the sea into Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tian Shenggong and Li Zhongchen by sea into Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以兵隸神策，為京西兵馬使，鎮奉天。

translations.literal: An edict assigned his troops to the Shence Army; he became Capital-West Army Supervisor and garrisoned Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred his troops to the Shence Army; he was made Capital-West army supervisor and stationed at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗初立，稍繩諸節度跋扈者。

translations.literal: When Dezong first ascended, he gradually restrained the various military commissioners who were overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first took the throne, he began reining in the overbearing military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 於是李正己屯曹州，田悅增河上兵，河南大擾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Zhengyi encamped at Cao Prefecture, Tian Yue increased troops on the Yellow River, and Henan was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi then encamped at Caozhou, Tian Yue reinforced his troops along the Yellow River, and Henan fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔移兵萬二千戍關東，帝御望春樓誓師，因勞遣諸將。

translations.literal: An edict moved twelve thousand troops to garrison Guandong; the Emperor attended at Wangchun Tower to swear in the army and thereupon consoled and dispatched the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered twelve thousand troops east to garrison Guandong. The emperor reviewed them at Wangchun Tower, took the army oath, and then sent the generals off with words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 酒至神策，將士不敢飲。

translations.literal: When wine reached the Shence troops, the officers and soldiers did not dare to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine reached the Shence troops, the officers and men refused to drink.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，惠元曰：「初發奉天，臣之帥張巨濟與眾約：『是役也，不立功，毋飲酒！

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; Huiyuan said: "When we first set out from Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji made a pact with the masses: 'In this campaign, if we achieve no merit, do not drink wine!'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. Huiyuan said, "When we left Fengtian, my commander Zhang Juji made a pact with the men: 'In this campaign, whoever wins no merit shall not drink wine!'"

sentences.zh: 』臣不敢食其言。

translations.literal: I dare not eat my words."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not break that vow."

sentences.zh: 」既行，有饋於道，惟惠元軍瓶罍不發。

translations.literal: After they marched, there were gifts along the road; only Huiyuan's army did not open its jars and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, gifts of wine were offered along the road, but only Huiyuan's men kept their flasks sealed.

sentences.zh: 帝咨嘆不已，璽書慰勞。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in admiration without end and sent an imperial letter of consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at this repeatedly and sent an imperial letter of praise and consolation.

sentences.zh: 俄以兵三千會諸將擊田悅，戰御河，奪三橋，惠元功多。

translations.literal: Shortly with three thousand troops he joined the various generals to attack Tian Yue, fought at the Yu River, seized three bridges, and Huiyuan's achievements were many.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the other generals with three thousand men to attack Tian Yue, fought at the Yu River, captured three bridges, and won the greatest share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 以兵屬李懷光。

translations.literal: His troops were placed under Li Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were placed under Li Huai'guang's command.

sentences.zh: 及朱泚反，自河朔赴難，解奉天圍，加檢校工部尚書，攝貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he came from Hebei to relieve the crisis, lifted the siege of Fengtian, was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, and acted as Regional Inspector of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he marched from Hebei to the rescue, lifted the siege of Fengtian, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and named acting regional inspector of Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔惠元與神策行營節度使李晟、鄜坊節度使李建徽及懷光聯營便橋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Huiyuan, together with Li Sheng, military commissioner of the Shence field army, Li Jianhui, military commissioner of Zheng and Fang, and Huai'guang, to encamp jointly at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Huiyuan to camp jointly with Li Sheng, military commissioner of the Shence field army, Li Jianhui, military commissioner of Zheng and Fang, and Huai'guang at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 晟知懷光且叛，移屯東渭橋。

translations.literal: Sheng knew Huai'guang was about to rebel and moved his encampment to the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, knowing Huai'guang was on the verge of rebellion, shifted his camp to the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士陸贄諫帝曰：「四將接壘，晟等兵寡位下，為懷光所易，勢不兩完。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi remonstrated with the Emperor, saying: "The four generals' camps adjoin one another; Sheng and the others have few troops and lower rank, are easily handled by Huai'guang, and the situation cannot preserve both intact."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Lu Zhi urged the emperor, "With four generals camped side by side, Sheng and the others have fewer troops and lower rank; Huai'guang can easily overpower them, and both sides cannot survive intact."

sentences.zh: 晟既慮變，請與惠元東徙，則建徽孤立。

translations.literal: Since Sheng already feared change and requested to move east with Huiyuan, Jianhui would be isolated.
translations.idiomatic: If Sheng, fearing treachery, moves east with Huiyuan, Jianhui will be left isolated.

sentences.zh: 宜因晟行，合兩軍皆往，以備賊為解，趣裝進道，則懷光計無所施。

translations.literal: It is fitting to take advantage of Sheng's move and have both armies go together, using defense against the rebels as the explanation, urging equipment and advancing on the road — then Huai'guang's schemes would have nowhere to apply.
translations.idiomatic: You should use Sheng's move as the occasion to send both armies east together, citing the need to guard against the rebels, and order them to pack up and march at once — then Huai'guang's plot will come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，使神策將李升往伺。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow this; he sent Shence general Li Sheng to spy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed this advice and sent the Shence general Li Sheng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「懷光反明甚。

translations.literal: Returning he reported: "Huai'guang's rebellion is very clear."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported, "Huai'guang's rebellion is unmistakable."

sentences.zh: 」是夕，奪二軍，惠元、建徽走奉天，懷光遣將冉宗馳騎追及於好畤。

translations.literal: That evening he seized the two armies; Huiyuan and Jianhui fled to Fengtian; Huai'guang sent general Ran Zong with cavalry in pursuit and overtook them at Haozhi.
translations.idiomatic: That night Huai'guang seized both armies. Huiyuan and Jianhui fled toward Fengtian, and Huai'guang sent the general Ran Zong in pursuit; he overtook them at Haozhi.

sentences.zh: 惠元被髮呼天，血流出眥，袒裼戰而死。

translations.literal: Huiyuan let down his hair and cried to Heaven; blood flowed from the corners of his eyes; baring his torso he fought and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyuan tore loose his hair and cried to heaven, blood streaming from his eyes; stripped to the waist he fought until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 二子晟、暠匿井中，皆及害。

translations.literal: His two sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well; both met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Sheng and Gao hid in a well but were both killed.

sentences.zh: 建徽獨免。

translations.literal: Jianhui alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhui alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔贈惠元尚書左僕射，晟殿中監，暠邠州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Huiyuan Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Sheng Palace Supervisor, and Gao Regional Inspector of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Huiyuan Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Sheng palace supervisor, and Gao regional inspector of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少子旻，字公素。

translations.literal: His youngest son Min, courtesy name Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Min, whose courtesy name was Gongsu,

sentences.zh: 惠元之死，被八創，墮別井，或救得免。

translations.literal: At Huiyuan's death Min suffered eight wounds, fell into another well, and was rescued and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: when Huiyuan was killed, suffered eight wounds, fell into another well, and was pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 歷邢州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Regional Inspector of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as regional inspector of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盧從史既縛，潞軍潰，有驍卒五千，從史嘗以子視者，奔於旻，旻閉城不內。

translations.literal: After Lu Congshi was bound, the Lu army collapsed; there were five thousand fierce soldiers whom Congshi had once treated as sons; they fled to Min, and Min closed the city and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Congshi was captured, the Lu army collapsed. Five thousand elite troops whom Congshi had treated like sons fled to Min, but Min shut the gates and refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭曰：「奴失帥，今公有完城，又度支錢百萬在府，少賜之，為表天子求旌節。

translations.literal: The masses all wept, saying: "We slaves have lost our commander; now you, sir, have an intact city, and moreover a million strings of revenue funds are in the prefecture; grant us a little, and we will memorialize the Son of Heaven to request a command banner and staff."
translations.idiomatic: They all wept and said, "We have lost our commander, but you hold an intact city, and a million strings of revenue funds are stored in the prefecture. Give us a little, and we will petition the throne on your behalf for a military commission."

sentences.zh: 」旻開諭禍福遣之，眾感悟，遂還軍。

translations.literal: Min opened the gates, explained fortune and misfortune, and sent them away; the masses were moved to understanding and thereupon returned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Min opened the gates, explained the consequences to them, and sent them away. Moved by his words, they returned to their units.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之，遷易州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianzong commended him and transferred him to be Regional Inspector of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong praised him and transferred him to regional inspector of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王師討吳元濟，以唐州刺史提兵深入二百里，薄申州，拔外郛，殘其垣。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Wu Yuanji, as Regional Inspector of Tang Prefecture he led troops deep two hundred li, pressed close to Shen Prefecture, took the outer suburbs, and destroyed its walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he led his Tang Prefecture troops two hundred li into enemy territory, pressed Shenzhou, captured its outer suburbs, and tore down its walls.

sentences.zh: 以功加御史中丞。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 容州西原蠻反，授本州經略招討使，擊定之。

translations.literal: The Western Yuan barbarians of Rong Prefecture rebelled; he was appointed military commissioner and pacification commissioner of that prefecture and attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Yuan tribes of Rong Prefecture rebelled, he was made military commissioner and pacification commissioner of the prefecture and crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 進御史大夫，合邕、容兩管為一道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and merged the two circuits of Yong and Rong into one.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and merged the Yong and Rong circuits into a single command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Left Regular Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 李元諒

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang

sentences.zh: 李元諒，安息人。

translations.literal: Li Yuanliang was a man of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanliang was of Parthian descent.

sentences.zh: 本安氏，少為宦官駱奉先養息，冒姓駱，名元光。

translations.literal: Originally of the An clan, in youth he was adopted as a son by the eunuch Luo Fengxian, took the surname Luo falsely, and was named Yuanguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally of the An clan; as a youth the eunuch Luo Fengxian adopted him, and he took the surname Luo and the name Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，鷙敢有謀。

translations.literal: He had fine beard and whiskers, was fierce and bold, and possessed strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and full-bearded, he was fierce, daring, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 以宿衛積勞試太子詹事。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit in palace guard service he was tried as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Long service in the palace guard earned him appointment as acting Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李懷讓節度鎮國，署奏以自副。

translations.literal: When Li Huairang was military commissioner of Zhenguo, he appointed him in a memorial as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huairang served as military commissioner of Zhenguo, he named Yuanliang his deputy in a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 居軍十年，士心憚服。

translations.literal: He remained in the army ten years; the soldiers' hearts feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten years with the army, and the troops feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，賊遣將何望之襲華州，於是刺史董晉棄城走。

translations.literal: When Dezong went out to Fengtian, the rebels sent general He Wangzhi to raid Hua Prefecture; thereupon Regional Inspector Dong Jin abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong withdrew to Fengtian, the rebels sent the general He Wangzhi to strike Hua Prefecture, and the regional inspector Dong Jin abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 望之欲聚兵以絕東道，元諒自潼關引兵徑薄其城，拔之。

translations.literal: Wangzhi wished to gather troops to cut off the eastern route; Yuanliang led troops from Tong Pass directly to press his city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi planned to mass troops and sever the eastern route, but Yuanliang marched from Tong Pass straight against his position and recaptured the city.

sentences.zh: 時兵興倉卒，裹罽為鎧，剡蒿為矢，募兵數日至萬餘，軍氣乃振。

translations.literal: At the time the army arose in haste; they wrapped felt as armor and carved artemisia as arrows; within several days recruited troops reached more than ten thousand, and the army's spirit was then revived.
translations.idiomatic: The army had been raised in haste: felt was wrapped for armor and artemisia stalks carved into arrows. Within days he recruited more than ten thousand men, and the troops' morale revived.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻，輒卻。

translations.literal: When rebels came to attack, they were always repelled.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels attacked, he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時尚可孤守藍田，元諒屯昭應，王權壁中渭橋，賊兵不能逾渭南。

translations.literal: At the time Shang Ke'gu guarded Lantian, Yuanliang encamped at Zhaoying, Wang Quan fortified at the Middle Wei Bridge, and rebel troops could not cross south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ke'gu held Lantian, Yuanliang encamped at Zhaoying, and Wang Quan fortified the Middle Wei Bridge, so rebel forces could not cross south of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷鎮國軍節度使，封武康郡王。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Wukang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made military commissioner of the Zhenguo Army and created Prince of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔發豳、隴兵東討李希烈。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict had dispatched Bin and Long troops east to attack Li Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered Bin and Long troops east to campaign against Li Xilie.

sentences.zh: 師方出關，泚使劉忠孝召還；

translations.literal: The army had just left the pass when Zhu Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to summon them back;
translations.idiomatic: The army had just left the pass when Zhu Ci sent Liu Zhongxiao to recall them;

sentences.zh: 至華陰，華陰尉李夷簡說驛官捕之，追及關，元諒斬以徇，所召兵不得入，由是華州獨完。

translations.literal: reaching Huayin, Huayin Assistant Li Yijian persuaded the post-station official to seize him; pursuing to the pass, Yuanliang beheaded him and displayed the head; the summoned troops could not enter; thereby Hua Prefecture alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: but at Huayin the assistant Li Yijian persuaded the post officials to seize the messenger. Yuanliang overtook them at the pass, executed the envoy, and displayed his head, so the recalled troops could not enter. Hua Prefecture alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 俄詔元諒與李晟收京師，次浐西。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to recover the capital; they halted west of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Yuanliang and Li Sheng to retake the capital; they encamped west of Chan.

sentences.zh: 元諒先奮鏖賊，敗之，進屯苑東，晟使壞苑垣入。

translations.literal: Yuanliang first fought fiercely and wore down the rebels, defeated them, advanced to encamp east of the park, and Sheng had the park wall broken to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang led the fierce assault, routed the rebels, and advanced to camp east of the imperial park while Sheng breached the park wall to enter.

sentences.zh: 泚連戰皆北，遂大潰，京師平。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci fought repeatedly and was always defeated northward; thereupon he collapsed in great rout, and the capital was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci lost battle after battle and finally broke in full rout; the capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 讓功於晟，退壁近郊。

translations.literal: He yielded merit to Sheng and withdrew to fortify in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded the credit to Sheng and withdrew his forces to camp in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶五百，賜甲第、女樂、一子六品官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, granted five hundred households of actual fief, and given a fine mansion, female musicians, and one son a sixth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, granted an actual fief of five hundred households, and given a grand residence, female musicians, and a sixth-rank post for one son.

sentences.zh: 李懷光反，與馬燧、渾瑊討之。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he joined Ma Sui and Hun Jian to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he campaigned against him with Ma Sui and Hun Jian.

sentences.zh: 其將徐廷光素易元諒，數嫚罵，為優胡戲，斥侮其祖。

translations.literal: His general Xu Tingguang had always looked down on Yuanliang, repeatedly insulted and reviled him, made comic Sogdian performances, and denounced and humiliated his ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's general Xu Tingguang had long despised Yuanliang, repeatedly insulted him, staged comic performances mocking him, and reviled his ancestors.

sentences.zh: 又使約降，曰：「我降漢將耳。

translations.literal: He also sent to arrange surrender, saying: "I surrender only to a Han general."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent to negotiate surrender, saying, "I will surrender only to a Han general."

sentences.zh: 」及馬燧至，降於燧。

translations.literal: When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui arrived, he surrendered to Sui instead.

sentences.zh: 元諒見韓遊瑰曰：「彼詬吾祖，今日斬之，子助我乎？

translations.literal: Yuanliang saw Han Yougui and said: "He reviled my ancestors; today I shall behead him — will you help me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang went to Han Yougui and said, "He insulted my ancestors. I mean to kill him today — will you help me?"

sentences.zh: 」許諾。

translations.literal: He promised.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而遇諸道，即數其罪，叱左右斬之，詣燧謝。

translations.literal: Thereupon meeting the various circuit representatives, he immediately enumerated his crimes, shouted to his attendants to behead him, and went to Sui to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied commanders met, he at once listed Xu's crimes, ordered his attendants to execute him, and then went to apologize to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧大怒，將殺元諒，遊瑰見曰：「殺一偏裨尚爾，即殺一節度，法宜如何？

translations.literal: Sui was greatly angered and was about to kill Yuanliang; Yougui saw him and said: "If killing a subordinate general is like this, then killing a military commissioner — how would the law stand?"
translations.idiomatic: Sui was furious and was about to execute Yuanliang. Yougui intervened: "If you react this way to the killing of a subordinate, what would the law say if you killed a military commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 」燧默然。

translations.literal: Sui was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Sui fell silent.

sentences.zh: 元諒請輸錢百萬勞軍自贖，瑊亦為請，燧赦之。

translations.literal: Yuanliang requested to contribute a million strings of cash to reward the army and redeem himself; Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang offered a million strings of cash to reward the army in atonement; Jian also pleaded for him, and Sui pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 帝以專殺，恐有司劾治，前詔勿論。

translations.literal: Because of unauthorized killing, the Emperor feared the authorities would impeach and punish him; an earlier edict ordered that it not be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the authorities would prosecute him for unauthorized execution, the emperor issued an advance edict that the matter was not to be pursued.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，吐蕃請盟，詔以軍從瑊會平涼，元諒軍潘原、遊瑰軍洛口以為援。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan the Tibetans requested alliance; an edict ordered troops to follow Jian to meet at Pingliang; Yuanliang's army at Panyuan and Yougui's army at Luokou were to serve as support.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3, when Tibet requested a treaty, an edict ordered troops to accompany Jian to Pingliang, with Yuanliang's army at Panyuan and Yougui's at Luokou as reserves.

sentences.zh: 元諒曰：「潘原去平涼七十里，虜詐不情，如有急，何以赴？

translations.literal: Yuanliang said: "Panyuan is seventy li from Pingliang; the barbarians are deceitful and insincere; if there is urgency, how can we go to help?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang said, "Panyuan is seventy li from Pingliang. The Tibetans are treacherous. If trouble comes, how can we reach you in time?"

sentences.zh: 請與公連屯。

translations.literal: I request to encamp jointly with you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we camp together."

sentences.zh: 」瑊以違詔，不聽。

translations.literal: Jian, because it violated the edict, did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused, citing the edict's orders.

sentences.zh: 瑊壁盟所二十里，元諒密徙營次之。

translations.literal: Jian fortified twenty li from the alliance site; Yuanliang secretly moved his camp next to it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian encamped twenty li from the treaty site, but Yuanliang quietly moved his camp beside him.

sentences.zh: 既會，元諒望雲物曰：「不詳，虜必有變！

translations.literal: After they met, Yuanliang looked at the clouds and omens and said: "This is inauspicious; the barbarians must have a change!"
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting Yuanliang studied the sky and said, "This is ill-omened — the Tibetans must be plotting something!"

sentences.zh: 」傳令約部伍出陣。

translations.literal: He transmitted orders for the units to form battle lines and go out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his units to form up for battle.

sentences.zh: 俄而虜劫盟，瑊奔還，元諒兵成列出，而涇原節度使李觀亦以精兵五千伏險，與元諒相表裏，虜騎乃解。

translations.literal: Shortly the barbarians raided the alliance; Jian fled back; Yuanliang's troops formed ranks and went out; moreover Jingyuan military commissioner Li Guan also with five thousand elite troops lay in ambush in difficult terrain, coordinating inside and outside with Yuanliang, and the barbarian cavalry thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tibetans broke the treaty. Jian fled, but Yuanliang's troops were already in battle order. Li Guan, military commissioner of Jingyuan, had five thousand elite troops in ambush, coordinating with Yuanliang from both sides, and the Tibetan cavalry withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元諒遣車重先，而與瑊振旅徐還，時以為有古良將風。

translations.literal: Yuanliang sent the baggage train ahead, while he and Jian rallied the army and returned slowly; at the time he was thought to have the manner of ancient good generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang sent the baggage train ahead and withdrew slowly with Jian in good order; contemporaries said he showed the bearing of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 是會也，微元諒、觀二人，瑊且不免。

translations.literal: At this meeting, but for the two men Yuanliang and Guan, Jian would scarcely have escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At that conference, had it not been for Yuanliang and Guan, Jian would scarcely have escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆，賜善馬金幣良厚，因賜姓及名。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and sighed in admiration, granted fine horses and gold and coins in great abundance, and thereupon granted him surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly and gave him fine horses and generous gifts of gold and coin, and bestowed on him the imperial surname and the name Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 更節度隴右，治良原。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be military commissioner of Longyou and governed at Liangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as military commissioner of Longyou with his headquarters at Liangyuan.

sentences.zh: 良原隍堞湮圮，旁皆平林薦草，虜入寇，常牧馬休徒於此。

translations.literal: At Liangyuan the moats and battlements were buried and ruined; on all sides were level woods and lush grass; when barbarians invaded, they often pastured horses and rested troops here.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyuan's walls and moats were in ruins, and level woods and tall grass surrounded the site where invaders often pastured horses and rested their men.

sentences.zh: 元諒培高浚淵，身執苦與士卒均，菑翳榛莽，辟美田數十里，勸士墾藝，歲入粟菽數十萬斛，什具畢給。

translations.literal: Yuanliang raised the heights and deepened the moats, personally took hardship equal to the soldiers, cleared overgrown brambles and thickets, opened fine fields for several tens of li, urged the soldiers to reclaim and cultivate, and yearly income of grain and beans reached several hundred thousand hu; all equipment was fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang raised the ramparts and deepened the moats, sharing the hard labor with his men. He cleared the brush, opened fine fields for miles around, and urged the troops to farm. Annual harvests reached hundreds of thousands of hu of grain and beans, and all equipment was fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 又築連弩臺，遠烽偵，為守備，進據勢勝，列新壁。

translations.literal: He also built repeating-crossbow towers, distant beacon and scout posts, made defensive preparations, advanced to occupy advantageous terrain, and arrayed new walls.
translations.idiomatic: He built repeating-crossbow towers, extended beacon and scout lines, strengthened the defenses, seized commanding ground, and erected new walls.

sentences.zh: 虜至無所掠，戰又輒北，由是涇、隴以安，西戎憚之。

translations.literal: When barbarians came there was nothing to plunder, and in battle they were always defeated northward; thereby Jing and Long were secured, and the western Rong feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came they found nothing to plunder and were repeatedly driven back. Jing and Long were secured, and the western tribes feared him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈司空，謚曰莊威。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two; posthumously he was made Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Zhuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Zhuangwei.

sentences.zh: 李觀，其先自趙郡徙洛陽，故為洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Guan: his ancestors moved from Zhao Commandery to Luoyang, and therefore he was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan's family had moved from Zhao Commandery to Luoyang, so he was counted as a man of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 少沈厚寡言。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep, steady, and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was grave, steady, and sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 以策干朔方節度使郭子儀，子儀遣佐坊州刺史吳伷為防遏使。

translations.literal: With a policy memorial he approached Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi; Ziyi sent him to assist Fang Prefecture Regional Inspector Wu Xian as defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a policy memorial to Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, who sent him to assist Wu Xian, regional inspector of Fang Prefecture, as defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以親喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of parental mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃內寇，代宗幸陜，觀隱盩厔，率鄉里子姓千人守黑水，虜不敢侵。

translations.literal: When Tibetans invaded within the borders, Emperor Daizong visited Shan; Guan hid at Zhaozhi, led a thousand clansmen of his district to guard Heishui, and the barbarians did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the interior, Emperor Daizong withdrew to Shan. Guan remained at Zhaozhi and led a thousand local clansmen to hold Heishui, and the enemy did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使楊慎微奏為偏將，徐浩、李勉代節度，常倚以軍政，數捕平劇賊。

translations.literal: Lingnan military commissioner Yang Shenwei memorialized him as a subordinate general; Xu Hao and Li Mian succeeded as military commissioners and constantly relied on him for military affairs, repeatedly capturing and pacifying fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenwei, military commissioner of Lingnan, recommended him as a subordinate general. Xu Hao and Li Mian, who succeeded as commissioners, relied on him for military affairs and repeatedly crushed major bandit gangs.

sentences.zh: 遷大將，試殿中監，召為右龍武將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to great general, tried as Palace Supervisor, and summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior commander, named acting palace supervisor, and summoned as Right Dragon Martial General.

sentences.zh: 涇師叛，觀適番上，即領兵千餘扈德宗奉天。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops rebelled, Guan happened to be on palace duty rotation; he immediately led more than a thousand troops to escort Dezong to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou troops mutinied, Guan happened to be on palace guard duty and at once led more than a thousand men to escort Dezong to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 詔盡察諸軍，整飭誰邏，增募五千人，鼙旝歡豎，士氣益振。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to inspect all armies fully, put in order the night patrols, increase recruitment by five thousand men; drums and banners were joyfully raised, and the soldiers' spirit was further revived.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put him in charge of inspecting all armies, tightening night patrols and recruiting five thousand more men. Drums and banners were raised in celebration, and morale surged.

sentences.zh: 賜封戶二百，授二子八品官。

translations.literal: He was granted two hundred fief households and two sons eighth-rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: He received a fief of two hundred households and eighth-rank posts for two sons.

sentences.zh: 從至梁州。

translations.literal: He followed to Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝還，詔總後軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, an edict ordered him to command the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, an edict named him commander of the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 擢四鎮、北庭行軍涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Beiting field army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Beiting field army.

sentences.zh: 在屯四年，訓部伍，儲藏饒衍。

translations.literal: He remained at his encampment four years, trained the units, and stores were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He spent four years at his post, drilling the ranks until stores overflowed.

sentences.zh: 平涼之盟，吐蕃不得志。

translations.literal: At the Pingliang alliance the Tibetans did not achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang treaty the Tibetans failed to achieve their aims.

sentences.zh: 是年，觀入朝，前一日就道，虜至期出精騎狙擊，不及，去。

translations.literal: That year Guan entered court; the day before he set out on the road, the barbarians arrived on schedule and sent elite cavalry to ambush and strike; they did not reach him in time and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Guan set out for court, the Tibetans sent elite cavalry to ambush him on the road the day before he departed, but they arrived too late and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以少府監檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Minister of Works with the post of Director of the Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting Minister of Works while serving as Director of the Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰

translations.literal: Han Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui

sentences.zh: 韓遊瑰，靈州靈武人，始為郭子儀裨將。

translations.literal: Han Yougui was a man of Lingwu in Ling Prefecture; he began as a subordinate general under Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui came from Lingwu in Ling Prefecture and began his career as a subordinate general under Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使阿史那從禮將同羅、突厥五千騎偽降於朔方，出塞門，誘河曲九蕃府、六胡叛，部落凡五十萬。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli to lead five thousand riders of Tongluo and Turks in feigned surrender to Shuofang, out through Saimen, to entice the Nine Tribal Offices and Six Hu of Hequ to rebel — tribes totaling five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Ashina Congli with five thousand Tongluo and Turk cavalry in a feigned surrender to Shuofang. They left through Saimen and incited the Nine Tribal Offices and Six Hu of Hequ to revolt — five hundred thousand tribesmen in all.

sentences.zh: 子儀使遊瑰率辛京杲擊破之，九蕃府還附。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Yougui leading Xin Jinggao to defeat and break them; the Nine Tribal Offices returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent Yougui with Xin Jinggao to rout them, and the Nine Tribal Offices returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 累進邠寧節度留後。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to acting military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 奉天之狩，兵未集，遊瑰與慶州刺史論惟明以兵三千來赴，自乾陵北趨醴泉，未至，有詔引軍屯便橋。

translations.literal: At the imperial hunt at Fengtian the armies were not yet gathered; Yougui and Qing Prefecture Regional Inspector Lun Weiming came with three thousand troops from north of Qianling toward Liquan; before they arrived, an edict ordered the army withdrawn to encamp at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Fengtian before his forces had assembled, Yougui and Lun Weiming, regional inspector of Qing Prefecture, marched three thousand men from north of Qianling toward Liquan. Before they arrived, an edict ordered them to encamp at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 次泥泉，與泚兵值，遊瑰欲還奉天，監軍翟文秀曰：「吾壁於此，賊敢逾我而西，可夾攻取之。

translations.literal: Halting at Niquan, they encountered Zhu Ci's troops; Yougui wished to return to Fengtian; army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said: "If we fortify here, when rebels dare pass us to go west, we can attack them from both sides and take them."
translations.idiomatic: At Niquan they met Zhu Ci's army. Yougui wanted to fall back to Fengtian, but the army supervisor Zhai Wenxiu said, "If we hold here and the rebels try to pass us westward, we can take them in a pincer."

sentences.zh: 今入奉天，賊亦隨至，是引賊迫天子也。

translations.literal: If we now enter Fengtian, the rebels will also follow and arrive — this is leading rebels to press upon the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If we enter Fengtian now, the rebels will follow and drive straight at the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」遊瑰曰：「不然，我寡賊眾。

translations.literal: Yougui said: "Not so — we are few, the rebels many."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui replied, "No. We are few and they are many."

sentences.zh: 彼分以亢我，餘眾猶能鼓而西也，不如先入衛天子。

translations.literal: If they divide to oppose us, the remaining masses can still drum and advance west; it is better first to enter and guard the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If they detach a force to block us, the rest can still march west. We should enter Fengtian first and protect the emperor."

sentences.zh: 且奉天無強卒，安得夾攻？

translations.literal: Moreover Fengtian has no strong troops — how can there be attack from both sides?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Fengtian has no strong garrison — how could we mount a pincer attack?"

sentences.zh: 吾士乏且寒，賊以利誘之，眾且潰。

translations.literal: Our soldiers are weary and cold; if the rebels entice them with profit, the masses will soon collapse."
translations.idiomatic: Our men are exhausted and cold. If the enemy tempts them with rewards, the ranks will break."

sentences.zh: 」遂還奉天。

translations.literal: Thereupon they returned to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 泚兵躡攻之，戰不利；

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's troops pursued and attacked them; the battle went unfavorably;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's troops pursued and attacked; the fighting went badly.

sentences.zh: 泚兵奪門，遊瑰殊死戰，乃解。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's troops seized the gate; Yougui fought to the death, and only then was the crisis relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized a gate, but Yougui fought with desperate valor until the attack was beaten off.

sentences.zh: 泚大治戰棚、雲橋，士皆懼，遊瑰曰：「賊取佛祠幹木為攻具，可以火之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci greatly prepared battle sheds and cloud bridges; the soldiers were all afraid; Yougui said: "The rebels take dry timber from Buddhist shrines for assault engines — they can be burned."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci built siege towers and assault bridges, and the troops were terrified. Yougui said, "The rebels are using dry timber from Buddhist shrines for their engines — we can burn them."

sentences.zh: 」既而賊大噪攻南雉，遊瑰曰：「是分吾力也。

translations.literal: Shortly the rebels made a great clamor attacking the southern bastion; Yougui said: "This divides our strength."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels launched a major assault on the southern bastion, Yougui said, "They are dividing our strength."

sentences.zh: 」趨北雉，遣將郭詢、郭廷玉以銳士三百傅滿直出，火其棚，投薪於中，風返，棚皆燼，賊氣沮。

translations.literal: He hurried to the northern bastion, sent generals Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred elite troops carrying full fuel to go straight out, set fire to their sheds, threw fuel within; the wind reversed, the sheds were all burned to ash, and the rebels' spirit was discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to the northern bastion and sent Guo Xun and Guo Tingyu with three hundred picked men carrying fuel straight at the enemy works. They set the sheds ablaze and threw in more fuel; the wind shifted back, the structures burned to ash, and rebel morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 故諸將推遊瑰赴難功第一。

translations.literal: Therefore the various generals ranked Yougui first in merit for going to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: The generals therefore ranked Yougui first in merit for the relief of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝以衛軍無職局，軍置統軍一員，以遊瑰、惟明、賈隱林處之。

translations.literal: Because the guard army had no command structure, the army established one post of army commander; Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin were placed in it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the palace guard lacked a command structure, the emperor created a post of army commander and appointed Yougui, Weiming, and Jia Yinlin to it.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛，誘遊瑰為變，遊瑰白髮其書。

translations.literal: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he enticed Yougui to mutiny; Yougui reported and displayed his letter.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled, he tried to win Yougui to his side; Yougui reported the plot and produced Huai'guang's letter.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿可謂忠義矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You may be called loyal and righteous!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have shown true loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣安知忠義？

translations.literal: He replied: "How would your servant know loyalty and righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "How would I know loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 但懷光誤臣，使震驚乘輿，後持臣自解。

translations.literal: Only Huai'guang misled your servant, causing alarm to the imperial carriage; afterward he would hold your servant up to excuse himself."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang misled me into alarming the imperial carriage, and would later have used me to excuse himself."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其誠，從問：「計欲安出？

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his sincerity and followed by asking: "What plan do you wish to put forth?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his candor and asked, "What do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「懷光總諸府兵，怙以為亂。

translations.literal: He replied: "Huai'guang commands the troops of the various prefectures and relies on them to make rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Huai'guang commands the troops of many prefectures and relies on them to rebel."

sentences.zh: 今邠有張昕，靈武有寧薍景璿，河中有呂鳴嶽，振武有杜從政，潼關有李朝臣，渭北有竇覦，皆守將也。

translations.literal: Now at Bin there is Zhang Xin, at Lingwu Ning Zhi Jingxuan, at Hezhong Lü Mingyue, at Zhenwu Du Congzheng, at Tong Pass Li Zhaochen, at Weibei Dou Kan — all are garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xin holds Bin, Jingxuan holds Lingwu, Lü Mingyue holds Hezhong, Du Congzheng holds Zhenwu, Li Zhaochen holds Tong Pass, and Dou Kan holds Weibei — all loyal garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 陛下以其眾與地授之，罷懷光權，而尊以元功，諸將仰首，各聽其帥，彼安能以亂？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should grant them their masses and territories, remove Huai'guang's authority, yet honor him with the title of foremost merit; the various generals will look up; each will obey his own commander — how can they make rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Give each commander his troops and territory, strip Huai'guang of power but honor him as foremost in merit. The generals will look to their own leaders — how could they follow him in rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「罷懷光權而泚益張，若何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If we remove Huai'guang's authority and Zhu Ci grows stronger, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "If we strip Huai'guang of power, Zhu Ci will grow stronger — what then?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下約士以不次之賞，今貢賦方至，發而酬之，其守自固。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has promised the soldiers extraordinary rewards; now tribute and levies are just arriving — distribute them in payment, and their defense will secure itself."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has promised extraordinary rewards. Tribute is arriving now — distribute it at once, and the garrisons will hold firm on their own."

sentences.zh: 邠有萬精甲，臣得將之，可以誅賊。

translations.literal: At Bin there are ten thousand elite armored troops; if your servant may lead them, the rebels can be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Bin has ten thousand elite armored troops. Give me command of them, and I can destroy the rebels."

sentences.zh: 四方杖義而起，賊不足慮。

translations.literal: From the four directions men rose bearing righteousness; the rebels are not worth anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal forces are rising everywhere on principle — the rebels are nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」帝美其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 會懷光誘復至，渾瑊得書，稍嚴卒以警。

translations.literal: When Huai'guang's enticements came again, Hun Jian received the letter and somewhat tightened the soldiers in warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang's overtures arrived again, Hun Jian received the letter and tightened discipline among his troops.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰不知，發怒，嫚罵瑊。

translations.literal: Yougui did not know; he grew angry and insulted and reviled Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui knew nothing of this and flew into a rage, hurling abuse at Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝疑有變，即日幸梁州，遊瑰使子從帝。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected a change and that very day visited Liang Prefecture; Yougui sent his son to follow the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting treachery, the emperor withdrew to Liang Prefecture the same day; Yougui sent his son to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 懷光檄假遊瑰邠州刺史，欲因張昕殺之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang issued a proclamation falsely appointing Yougui Regional Inspector of Bin Prefecture, wishing to use Zhang Xin to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang issued a proclamation naming Yougui regional inspector of Bin Prefecture, planning to have Zhang Xin kill him.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰既失兵，不知所圖。

translations.literal: Yougui having lost his army, did not know what plan to make.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his army, Yougui did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 有客劉南金說曰：「邠有留甲，可以立功，殆天假也！

translations.literal: A guest Liu Nanjin advised, saying: "At Bin there are troops left behind; merit can be achieved — perhaps Heaven lends this!"
translations.idiomatic: A retainer named Liu Nanjin said, "There are troops still at Bin. You can win merit there — perhaps Heaven is giving you the chance!"

sentences.zh: 」遊瑰悟，誘舊部兵八百馳入邠，說昕曰：「懷光自蹈禍機，公今可取富貴，無共汙不義也。

translations.literal: Yougui understood, enticed eight hundred old subordinate troops to gallop into Bin, and persuaded Xin, saying: "Huai'guang has himself stepped into the snare of disaster; you, sir, can now seize wealth and honor — do not together stain yourselves with unrighteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui took the hint, rallied eight hundred of his old troops, and rode into Bin. He told Xin, "Huai'guang has walked into disaster. You can seize fortune now — do not share in his treason."

sentences.zh: 我願以麾下為公先驅。

translations.literal: I wish to take my command as your vanguard, sir."
translations.idiomatic: I will lead my men as your vanguard."

sentences.zh: 」昕不聽。

translations.literal: Xin did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xin refused.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰移疾不出，陰結其將高固等。

translations.literal: Yougui feigned illness and did not go out, secretly joining with his generals Gao Gu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui claimed illness and stayed indoors while secretly winning over Xin's generals Gao Gu and others.

sentences.zh: 昕欲殺遊瑰，戒左右衷甲入。

translations.literal: Xin wished to kill Yougui and warned his attendants to wear armor beneath their robes when entering.
translations.idiomatic: Xin plotted to kill Yougui and ordered his attendants to wear armor under their robes.

sentences.zh: 昕小史李岌潛白遊瑰，伏甲先起，高固等應之，斬昕首以聞。

translations.literal: Xin's junior clerk Li Ji secretly informed Yougui; hidden armor rose first, Gao Gu and others responded, and they beheaded Xin and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's clerk Li Ji warned Yougui in secret. Yougui's men struck first; Gao Gu and the others joined in, beheaded Xin, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時懷光子玫在邠，遊瑰衛出之，曰：「殺之只以怒敵，至必遽，不如舍之。

translations.literal: At the time Huai'guang's son Mei was at Bin; Yougui guarded and escorted him out, saying: "Killing him would only anger the enemy; when he arrives he will hurry — better to spare him."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's son Mei was at Bin. Yougui escorted him out, saying, "Killing him would only enrage the enemy. When Huai'guang hears of it he will flee all the faster if we spare the boy."

sentences.zh: 」玫至涇陽，懷光遂走蒲州。

translations.literal: When Mei reached Jingyang, Huai'guang thereupon fled to Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei reached Jingyang, Huai'guang fled to Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰屯七盤，受李晟節度。

translations.literal: Yougui encamped at Qipan and accepted Li Sheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui encamped at Qipan and placed himself under Li Sheng's command.

sentences.zh: 詔拜邠寧節度使，遂會渾瑊於奉天，與瑊、戴休顏分扼京西要險。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Binning; he then joined Hun Jian at Fengtian, and with Jian and Dai Xiuyan divided control of the strategic passes west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him military commissioner of Binning. He joined Hun Jian at Fengtian and, with Jian and Dai Xiuyan, held the key passes west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 李晟入長安，遊瑰破泚兵咸陽。

translations.literal: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui defeated Zhu Ci's troops at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng entered Chang'an, Yougui routed Zhu Ci's forces at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 泚走涇州，遊瑰使諭涇將楊澄，澄拒不納，泚遂敗。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci fled to Jing Prefecture; Yougui sent to persuade Jing general Yang Cheng; Cheng refused to admit him, and Zhu Ci thereupon was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci fled to Jingzhou. Yougui sent envoys to the Jing commander Yang Cheng, who refused him entry, and Zhu Ci was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 京師平，遷檢校尚書左僕射，實封戶四百。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with four hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered, he was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with an actual fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝至自興元，遊瑰及瑊、休顏從，而李晟、尚可孤、李元諒奉迎，論功與瑊等皆第一。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived from Xingyuan, Yougui followed with Jian and Xiuyan, while Li Sheng, Shang Ke'gu, and Li Yuanliang came to welcome him; in reckoning merit they were all ranked first with Jian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Xingyuan, Yougui accompanied him with Jian and Xiuyan, while Li Sheng, Shang Ke'gu, and Li Yuanliang came out to welcome him. In the reckoning of merit they all ranked first with Jian.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰還屯邠寧。

translations.literal: Yougui returned to encamp at Binning.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui returned to his post at Binning.

sentences.zh: 懷光寇同州，瑊、元諒敗於乾坑。

translations.literal: Huai'guang raided Tong Prefecture; Jian and Yuanliang were defeated at Qiankeng.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang raided Tong Prefecture, and Jian and Yuanliang were defeated at Qiankeng.

sentences.zh: 詔遊瑰率兵並力，敗賊眾五千於屯。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yougui to lead troops in combined strength and defeat five thousand of the rebel masses at the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yougui to join the campaign; he defeated five thousand rebels at their camp.

sentences.zh: 遂會瑊、馬燧圍蒲城。

translations.literal: He thereupon joined Jian and Ma Sui in besieging Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Jian and Ma Sui in besieging Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 師次焦籬堡，守將尉珪降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jiaoli Fort; defending general Wei Gui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaoli Fort the defending general Wei Gui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 懷光見勢單蹙，乃縊死。

translations.literal: Huai'guang, seeing his position isolated and pressed, thereupon hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his position hopeless, Huai'guang hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，吐蕃入涇、隴、邠、寧，遊瑰追至安化，虜營合水北。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan Tibetans entered Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning; Yougui pursued to Anhua; the barbarians encamped north of the He River.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 the Tibetans raided Jing, Long, Bin, and Ning. Yougui pursued them to Anhua, where they camped north of the He River.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰策曰：「賊行無人地，必怠，可襲取之。

translations.literal: Yougui planned, saying: "The rebels march through uninhabited land and must grow slack; they can be taken by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said, "They are marching through empty country and will grow careless. We can take them by surprise."

sentences.zh: 」使將史履澄夜領兵五百入其營，斬數百級，取馬五千。

translations.literal: He sent general Shi Lücheng by night to lead five hundred troops into their camp, beheading several hundred and taking five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the general Shi Lücheng with five hundred men into the enemy camp by night. They killed several hundred Tibetans and captured five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 遲明，虜以兵尾擊，遊瑰羅幟自衛，鼙鼓四發，虜驚潰去。

translations.literal: At dawn the barbarians struck from the rear; Yougui arrayed banners to defend himself, drums and gongs sounded on four sides, and the barbarians fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Tibetans counterattacked from the rear. Yougui drew up his banners, drums sounded on every side, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復圍鹽州，刺史杜彥光約與之城，吐蕃許之，又取銀、夏、麟等州。

translations.literal: That year they again besieged Salt Prefecture; Regional Inspector Du Yanguang agreed to hand over the city to them; Tibet agreed and also took Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year they besieged Salt Prefecture again. The regional inspector Du Yanguang agreed to surrender the city, and Tibet also seized Yin, Xia, Lin, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰請收鹽州以斷戎人走集：「虜入漢，食禾菽，方春而病，此天亡時也。

translations.literal: Yougui requested to recover Salt Prefecture to cut off the Rong people's routes of flight and gathering: "When barbarians enter Han territory they eat grain and beans; it is just spring and they fall ill — this is the time Heaven destroys them."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui urged recovering Salt Prefecture to cut the enemy's lines of retreat: "When they invade Han territory they eat our grain and beans. It is spring and they fall sick — Heaven is destroying them."

sentences.zh: 」有詔李元諒、韓全義率師一萬，會遊瑰收鹽州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi each to lead ten thousand troops to join Yougui in recovering Salt Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Yuanliang and Han Quanyi each to bring ten thousand men and join Yougui in retaking Salt Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃請修清水盟，以歸侵地，馬燧為之請。

translations.literal: Tibet requested to renew the Qingshui alliance and return invaded territory; Ma Sui pleaded for this.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet asked to renew the Qingshui treaty and return conquered land; Ma Sui supported the request.

sentences.zh: 詔問遊瑰，答曰：「西戎弱則請盟，強則入寇。

translations.literal: An edict asked Yougui; he replied: "When the western Rong are weak they request alliance; when strong they invade."
translations.idiomatic: The throne asked Yougui, who answered, "When the western tribes are weak they sue for peace; when strong they raid."

sentences.zh: 今侵地益深而乞盟，詐我也！

translations.literal: Now they invade deeper yet beg for alliance — they are deceiving us!"
translations.idiomatic: They have seized more land than ever and now beg for a treaty — this is a trick!"

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會盟平涼，詔遊瑰以軍屯洛口。

translations.literal: When they met in alliance at Pingliang, an edict ordered Yougui to encamp his army at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: At the Pingliang conference an edict ordered Yougui to station his army at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 盟之日，遊瑰以勁騎五百待非常，令曰：「即有變，急趨柏泉以分虜勢。

translations.literal: On the day of the alliance, Yougui held five hundred elite cavalry in readiness for the unexpected, ordering: "If there is a change, hurry to Baiquan to divide the barbarians' strength."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the treaty Yougui held five hundred elite horsemen in reserve and ordered, "If anything goes wrong, ride at once for Baiquan to split the enemy force."

sentences.zh: 」瑊被劫，馳以免，虜見兵出，即解去。

translations.literal: Jian was seized in the raid and galloped to escape; the barbarians saw troops come out and thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was ambushed but rode clear; when the Tibetans saw troops advancing they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃寇大回原，遊瑰方壁長武，即選騎八百迎擊，自引兵繼之。

translations.literal: Later Tibetans raided Dayuan Plain; Yougui was then fortifying at Changwu; he immediately selected eight hundred cavalry to meet and strike them, himself leading troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tibet raided Dayuan Plain, Yougui was fortifying at Changwu. He sent eight hundred cavalry to intercept them and followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 監軍以為戎不可易，答曰：「賊攻豐義，今遊騎先破，則彼大眾不敢前，豐義全矣！

translations.literal: The army supervisor thought the Rong could not be lightly challenged; he replied: "The rebels are attacking Fengyi; if our roaming cavalry break them first, their great masses will not dare advance, and Fengyi will be preserved!"
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor said the enemy could not be challenged lightly. Yougui answered, "They are attacking Fengyi. If our cavalry defeat their scouts first, their main force will not dare advance and Fengyi will be saved."

sentences.zh: 」戰南原，敗之，吐蕃夜遁。

translations.literal: They fought on the southern plain, defeated them, and Tibet fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on the southern plain, routed them, and the Tibetans fled by night.

sentences.zh: 會子欽緒以射生將衛京師，與妖人李廣弘謀反，謀泄，奔邠州，中人捕斬，以狀示遊瑰。

translations.literal: His son Qinxu, as a bowman-captain guarding the capital, plotted rebellion with the sorcerer Li Guanghong; the plot leaked; he fled to Bin Prefecture; palace agents captured and beheaded him and showed the report to Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinxu, a bowman-captain guarding the capital, plotted rebellion with the charlatan Li Guanghong. The plot was exposed; he fled to Binzhou, was captured and executed by palace agents, and the report was sent to Yougui.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰懼，求歸死京師，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yougui was afraid and requested to return to die in the capital; the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui was terrified and asked to return to the capital to accept punishment; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又執欽緒二息送京師，帝亦原之。

translations.literal: He also seized Qinxu's two sons and sent them to the capital; the Emperor also pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Qinxu's two sons to the capital; the emperor pardoned them as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入朝，素服聽命，有詔復位，勞遇如故。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court, wore plain garments and awaited orders; an edict restored his position, and rewards and treatment were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he came to court in plain dress to await judgment. An edict restored him to office, and he was received with the same honors as before.

sentences.zh: 遊瑰盛言城豐義以遏虜侵。

translations.literal: Yougui strongly urged fortifying Fengyi to check barbarian invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui urged building a fortress at Fengyi to block enemy raids.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，趣還軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and urged him to return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 初，遊瑰之朝，眾謂且得罪，故賫送殊薄。

translations.literal: At first, when Yougui went to court, the masses said he would soon be punished; therefore gifts sent were especially meager.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui first went to court, his men expected him to be punished, so their parting gifts were meager.

sentences.zh: 既還，舉軍不自安。

translations.literal: After he returned, the whole army was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the whole army was uneasy.

sentences.zh: 大將范希朝善兵，遊瑰畏其逼，欲誅之，希朝奔鳳翔，帝聞，召入宿衛。

translations.literal: Great general Fan Xichao was skilled in warfare; Yougui feared his pressure and wished to execute him; Xichao fled to Fengxiang; when the Emperor heard, he summoned him into palace guard service.
